brief.headline: Annalee has withdrawn since a close friend died last month, missing 6 of 8 day center days and reporting feeling "down", and her spouse Marcus, her primary caregiver, is exhausted and asking for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 the day center reported Annalee missed 6 of the last 8 scheduled days. When she attends, she is quiet and leaves activities early. On 2026-10-28 she told the social worker she feels "down" and doesn't want to leave the house since a close friend died last month. The plan is to screen for depression and offer grief support.

items.statement: On 2026-11-12 Marcus, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in that window: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and readmissions, noting reason and discharge instructions.
Falls and near-falls: count any falls, mechanism, injuries, and whether a post-fall assessment was documented. Given age 90, check gait/balance notes and any fall-risk screen results.
Cardiac status: review any chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, syncope, or new heart failure symptoms; check whether cardiology or primary care follow-up occurred after the 2013 STEMI.

Medication reconciliation: compare the active list (aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, carvedilol 12.5 mg, lisinopril 5 mg, prasugrel 10 mg) against the window's prescribing and pharmacy fill records; flag any starts, stops, dose changes, or missed refills.

Antiplatelet review: prasugrel was started in 2013 and is still active; check the documented indication, duration, and any bleeding events, bruising, or GI bleeding noted in the window, and flag for prescriber review rather than recommending a change.

Blood pressure and heart rate trend across the window (lisinopril, carvedilol): look for hypotension, orthostatic symptoms, bradycardia, or readings outside documented targets; note any potassium or creatinine results if drawn.
Metabolic and weight trend: pull weights and BMI (obesity documented), and glucose or HbA1c results given prediabetes; note any change of 5% or more or new diabetes diagnosis.
Lab monitoring due: check whether lipid panel, renal function, potassium, and CBC (relevant to antiplatelet therapy) are current or overdue per the care plan.
Oral health and nutrition: review dental visits and any documented chewing difficulty, diet changes, or weight loss tied to tooth loss.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: review ADL/IADL changes, cognitive screening results, depression screening, social engagement or attendance at programs, caregiver availability and strain, and any care-plan items with due dates in or before 2026-11-30.
